After a year of intensive real estate expansion in the South Bay in 2025, Apple is once again enlarging its footprint in Sunnyvale. Here are the details.

Apple Continues to Expand Its Footprint

According to a report by The Mercury News (republished by AppleInsider), Apple has agreed to lease a 125,800-square-foot office building at 580 North Mary Avenue in Sunnyvale.

This transaction marks Apple's first major real estate move in the area in 2026. In 2025, the company spent more than US$1 billion expanding its footprint in the South Bay, making it an extremely busy year.

The expansion included acquiring the Cupertino Gateway complex—comprising three buildings—for US$166.9 million, the Mathilda Commons campus in Sunnyvale—consisting of two buildings—for US$350 million, and the adjacent Mathilda Campus—comprising four buildings—for US$365 million.

Apple subsequently spent an additional US$216 million on two buildings along Cupertino's Stevens Creek Boulevard, bringing its Bay Area expansion in 2025 to more than 1.5 million square feet of office and laboratory space.

Turning back to Apple's new lease, The Mercury News notes that this deal comes as office leasing activity in the South Bay is beginning to pick up, with vacancy rates improving both quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year:

According to a Colliers report, the office vacancy rate in the South Bay for the second quarter of 2026 stood at 14.1%. Colliers defines the market area as Santa Clara County and Fremont.

Besides Apple, the report also mentioned that Amazon has agreed to lease a total of 316,600 square feet of office space at 1000 Enterprise Way in Sunnyvale.
